title: Explore Inheritance — breeding screen layout
question: Three structures for the same screen, same palette throughout so the choice is composition only. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Generations Recede
options.thesis: Past generations shrink and dim upward while the live litter holds the floor.
options.viewport: Two faded generation strips above, breeding pair and tumbler centred, eight litter slots, counts and controls on the floor.
options.risk: The recede barely read at 1366x768: P and F1 look nearly equal, so the depth idea may not survive the build.

options.label: Ledger Spine
options.thesis: The pedigree is a ledger whose rows carry their own tallies, so the screen already looks like the sheet they copy onto.
options.viewport: A 452px ledger down the left, one row per generation with pair thumbs, kept dog's code and its counts inline; breeding stage fills the right.
options.risk: The ledger is dead weight on Day 1 when only one row exists, and it costs a third of the width forever.

options.label: Specimen Board
options.thesis: Four permanent columns, one per generation; the board never clears, so the whole experiment is visible at once.
options.viewport: P, F1, F2, F3 as full-height columns of dog tiles, each with its own counts table locked to the bottom.
options.risk: No stage for the fertilisation sequence: the tumbler has nowhere to live, and that animation is the emotional centre of the lesson.
